subject: Post-call: RTBF delegation playbook, archival locks & backup constraints
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Morris <janelle.m@finapps.com>, security@finapps.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: RTBF delegation playbook, archival locks & backup constraints

Hi Janelle / FinApps security team — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify the scope and put an executable plan on the table.

Summary from our discussion:
- Scope: customer-initiated user deletion (RTBF) for end-user personal data in request records and generated content. FinApps also needs deletion of per-user request logs and per-session metadata.
- Backups: you said weekly snapshot backups are retained for ~90 days and there are archival locks on some ledgers.
- KMS: preference for customer-managed keys for production data and backups.
- Evidence: you need proof-of-deletion (audit log entry + exported manifest) for compliance and a 3rd-party auditor.

Questions we need to confirm from your side (so we can size technical work / timeline):
1) Is the deletion request always at end-user level (email/uid) or sometimes account-wide (org scoped)? Please give the naming convention you use for user IDs.
2) Can you accept a 2-phase approach: (A) immediate deletion of active records and exclusion from restores, and (B) full cryptographic/key-revocation purge of backup copies within a maximum of 90 days?
3) Do the archival locks prevent key-rotation or crypto-erase of the underlying snapshots? (you mentioned ledger snapshots were under WORM policy)
4) Any procurement constraints for us holding short-term evidence exports (SFTP/secure link) vs. in-console logs?

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- Deliver a one-page RTBF delegation playbook (attached) that maps responsibilities: Redwood vs FinApps vs KMS provider.
- We will map the endpoints that perform user deletions and provide an API to request deletion programmatically (can be webhook or UI).
- Work with your ops/security to validate key-management model (CMK vs Redwood-managed).
- Provide a proposed timeline for active-data deletion (target: 48 hrs after request) and a backup purge plan aligned to your retention & archival constraints.

Can you confirm the above items 1–4 and indicate whether procurement wants us to sign an addendum for data disposition? If you prefer, we can convert the playbook into a short SOW for procurement review.

ATTACHMENTS: RTBF_playbook_v1.pdf (summary + checklist), finapps-kms-diagram.png (recommended key flows)

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Janelle Morris <janelle.m@finapps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finapps.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF delegation playbook, archival locks & backup constraints

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming answers inline: 

1) Deletion scope: typically user-level by uid (we use finapps_uid:<org>-<user>). Occasionally procurement or legal will request account-wide purges — rare.
2) Two-phase approach: acceptable. Key constraints: active/live data deletion must be completed within 48 hours. For backups, our policy today is weekly snapshots retained 90 days; archival ledgers have a WORM lock for 180 days for auditable transactions and cannot be altered. We need guidance on what Redwood can and cannot change for WORM-protected objects.
3) Archival locks: they prevent in-place deletion of the snapshot object. However, we do accept cryptographic erasure of keys for CMK-protected snapshots as a compensating control if the vendor supports key-rotation/revocation.
4) Evidence handling: procurement prefers SFTP delivery of manifests to their secure bucket for the first 12 months, then archived logs sent to auditor on request.

Additional items:
- We will require an SLA addendum confirming 48-hr active-data deletion and a plan for backup non-availability/exclusion from restores within the first snapshot cycle post-request.
- One practical ask: can Redwood provide a signed deletion manifest (hash + timestamp) and an audit log entry showing the deletion operation and the operator id?

If you can draft the addendum (or a short SOW) with the proposed language about cryptographic erasure and the backup exception workflow, I can share with legal and procurement for review.

Thanks — Janelle
Janelle Morris | Head of Security | FinApps Inc.
janelle.m@finapps.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: RTBF delegation playbook, archival locks & backup constraints

Ben / Tessa — forwarding FinApps reply. Important negotiation points: 48-hr active deletion SLA, backups retained 90 days with some WORM-locked snapshots where they accept key-revocation as compensating control. Procurement wants SFTP delivery of manifests.

Suggested commercial approach: 
- Offer the 48-hr active-delete SLA in a limited-scope addendum (customer-activated per-deal) with a 30% premium on Reserved capacity during the SLO window OR include in enterprise support if they go Dedicated.
- For backups: Offer a documented cryptographic-erase procedure for CMK-managed backups + an evidence package (signed manifest + audit log) and a recommended statement noting that WORM-protected ledger objects cannot be removed but will be crypto-erased or excluded from restores.

Ask: Ben, can you draft a short addendum language for the SLO + evidence deliverable? Tessa, can you confirm whether CS/ops can support SFTP manifest delivery for 12 months?

Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Morris <janelle.m@finapps.com>, security@finapps.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: RTBF delegation playbook, archival locks & backup constraints

Janelle — thanks for the clear answers. Per our internal alignment, here is the concrete proposal and immediate action items: 

Proposal (high level)
- Active data: Redwood will delete active user records and logs within 48 hours of a valid RTBF request. We will provide a signed deletion manifest (SHA256 list of deleted object ids + timestamp) delivered to your SFTP endpoint and a corresponding audit-log entry in the Redwood Console.
- Backups & archival: For non-WORM snapshots, Redwood will support crypto-erase via CMK revocation or key-scramble within one snapshot cycle (i.e., before the next weekly snapshot completes). For WORM-locked ledger snapshots, we cannot alter the object in-place; instead we will: 
  * Exclude the user’s data from any future restores and mark records as non-recoverable in the log;
  * Provide cryptographic evidence of key-revocation where applicable;
  * Deliver an attestation describing the scope and limitations.
- Evidence delivery: Signed manifest + audit-log entry delivered to your SFTP bucket for 12 months. We will also keep a vendor-side copy for audit purposes for the same period.

Action items / timeline
- Today: Redwood to send a draft addendum (SLA + evidence language) and updated RTBF playbook (attached).
- 48 hours: FinApps to confirm SFTP credentials and UID naming convention (finapps_uid format).
- 5 business days: Redwood to present a technical runbook with endpoint names and sample API calls for programmatic deletion.

Caveats and notes
- If FinApps requires immediate purge of WORM-protected snapshot objects, we need a legal exception from the snapshot vendor or a signed acceptance of compensating controls (crypto-erase + attestation).
- For customer-managed KMS: We will perform the crypto-erase workflow in coordination with your KMS admin; full cryptographic unrecoverability depends on your KMS provider’s capabilities.

ATTACHMENTS: RTBF_playbook_v1.pdf (updated), finapps-kms-diagram.png
DOCUSIGN: https://docusign.com/FA-2027-034-sla (draft addendum)

If that aligns, we’ll push the addendum draft to DocuSign and loop legal/procurement. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk procurement through the SFTP manifest format — propose Thu 10am PT.

Best — Marissa
